title: Truth-up do prompt do orquestrador: dispatch/sidecar/handoff + boot le tail do journal
description: Auditoria 2026-07-08 achou o subagent-orchestrator.md (ambas copias) descrevendo um sistema que nao existe mais. CRITICAL: (a) dispatch protocol L165-174 diz que os 5 thin-proxies injetam slash via send-keys; real: plan/next/ship escrevem sinal em .claude/cam-loop.local.md (plan.ts:219, next.ts, ship.ts), so review/issue injetam; (b) L224-227 diz que /cam-plan e /cam-ship rodam no contexto do orquestrador e retornam result line; real: so escrevem sinal, runners deterministicos executam. STALE: L151 manda spawnar /cam-next em loop ate CAM_LOOP_STATUS=COMPLETE (sentinel inexistente; cam next e one-shot, sidecar loopa e pusha report); L195-206 reviewer descrito como 3rd-pane TUI worker (real: Task in-context via allowlist) e worker self-pusha summary (real: sidecar pusha, worker-report.ts:12-15); L42 allowlist do hook subdeclarado (real: Explore, Plan, claude-code-guide, planner, auditor, reviewer em orch-agent-allowlist.sh:63); L254-264 manda fechar issue no ship (real: ship JA auto-fecha, ship-pr.ts:163-175, risco double-close); L339/346 handoff required fields superdeclarados (handoff.ts:91-101 so exige schemaVersion/writtenAt/reason; projectContext opcional nao documentado); L337 HANDOFF_DUE emitido em TODO append com sucesso (index.ts:1552), so --cycle-close arma recycle; L178-182 issueNumber nao e gate do supervisor (so consumido no ship). OMISSION: meta_loop=auto (sidecar auto-planeja proximo issue, sidecar.ts:196-208), auto-file de SUGGESTIONs CAM-189 (backlog ganha issues que o orquestrador nao criou), rehydrate CAM_ORCH_REHYDRATE como step-0 do boot. CONTEXTO: boot step 3 manda ler journal.md INTEIRO (178KB, ~44k tok, 77% do boot); mudar pra tail (~10 entradas) + grep-on-demand pra ciclos antigos. Origem: auditoria de prompts 2026-07-08.

spec.scope: Comprehensive truth-up of the orchestrator prompt to match the real system, in BOTH copies (.claude/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md and templates/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md) plus re-embed into src/vendor/_generated.ts via `bun run embed-vendor`. Also changes the boot journal-read guidance from full-file to tail+grep-on-demand. Out of scope: --agent runtime enforcement (CAM-227), orchestrator context/window backstop (CAM-172), planner/auditor prompt staleness (CAM-228/230), implementer prompt (CAM-229).
acceptanceCriteria: Both orchestrator prompt copies no longer reference the CAM_LOOP_STATUS=COMPLETE sentinel and no longer instruct looping /cam-next until it; the dispatch protocol states that plan/next/ship write a signal to .claude/cam-loop.local.md and only review/issue inject a slash command via send-keys.

Both copies describe the reviewer as a Task-in-context worker (spawned under the PreToolUse allowlist) whose summary line is pushed by the sidecar (worker-report), NOT as a 3rd-pane TUI worker that self-pushes.
The allowlist reference in the prompt lists the full set enforced by orch-agent-allowlist.sh (Explore, Plan, claude-code-guide, subagent-planner, subagent-auditor, subagent-reviewer), not a subset.

The self-handoff section states only schemaVersion, writtenAt, and reason are required fields (matching handoff.ts), documents projectContext as optional, and states HANDOFF_DUE is armed only by `cam journal append --cycle-close`, not by every successful append.
The boot section documents CAM_ORCH_REHYDRATE as step 0 (rehydrate vs cold-boot), the meta_loop=auto sidecar auto-plan behavior, and CAM-189 auto-filed SUGGESTIONs appearing in the backlog.
The boot journal step reads only the tail (~10 most recent entries) with grep-on-demand for older cycles, not the entire journal.md.

The close-on-ship text states ship auto-closes the issue (ship-pr.ts) and that orchestrator manual close is a documented fallback only (used when the sidecar auto-close was skipped, e.g. a stale binary); the unconditional close-on-ship instruction is removed to prevent double-close.
issueNumber is described accurately (consumed at ship, not a supervisor gate).
`bun run embed-vendor:check` passes (re-embed applied), and `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` are green.
gotchas: Dual-copy is per-file and NOT guaranteed byte-identical; diff the two copies before assuming an edit forces re-embed (memory: cam-dual-copy-is-per-file).
embed-vendor:check is a required gate here because templates/ is touched; regenerate with `bun run embed-vendor` before committing.
The orchestrator is spawned without --agent, so its frontmatter is advisory only; do NOT try to fix the Write/disallowedTools contradiction here (that is CAM-227).
This is a prompt-only change; no src/ runtime behavior changes. The journal-tail is guidance the orchestrator follows at boot, not a code path.
